stem:
Prenol is a naturally occurring organic molecule found in many fruits. It contains both an alkene and an alcohol functional group.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Prenol can be formed by the reaction of $\mathbf{G}$ with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$.

Complete the diagram to show the mechanism of the reaction between $\mathbf{G}$ and $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ to form prenol.

Include all relevant charges, partial charges, lone pairs and curly arrows.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Prenol reacts with steam to form a mixture of three isomers, $\mathbf{J}$, $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{L}$, of molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
When $\mathbf{J}$ is heated with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI) it forms an organic product which shows no reaction with 2,4-DNPH.

Draw the structure of $\mathbf{J}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem:
$\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{L}$ are stereoisomers with molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$.

$\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{L}$ both react when heated with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI) to form $\mathbf{M}$, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$.

$\mathbf{M}$ forms an orange precipitate on reaction with 2,4-DNPH.
parts.text: Give the structural formula of $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{L}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Name the type of stereoisomerism shown by $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{L}$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Give the balanced equation to represent the reaction of $\mathbf{K}$, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$, with acidified potassium dichromate(VI) to form $\mathbf{M}$, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$.

Use $[\text{O}]$ to represent an atom of oxygen provided by the oxidising agent.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Prenol contains an alkene functional group.

Describe a chemical test to confirm the presence of an alkene functional group. Give the result of the test.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Prenol can be polymerised to form poly(prenol).

Draw **one** repeat unit of poly(prenol).

parts.label: (d)
(d)(ii)
parts.text:
Isoprenol is a liquid.

$\text{Ni}$ acts as a catalyst for reaction $\mathbf{1}$.

Identify the type of catalysis shown by $\text{Ni}$ in reaction $\mathbf{1}$.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Draw the **skeletal** formula of $\mathbf{Q}$ and suggest one commercial use of $\mathbf{Q}$.

{{figure:pdf_visual_05.png}}

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
The progress of reaction $\mathbf{I}$ can be monitored using infra-red spectroscopy.

One absorption that can be used to monitor the progress of this reaction is that of $\text{C-Cl}$ at $730\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

Identify another absorption that can be used to monitor the progress of this reaction. In your answer, you should refer to the specific bond and its corresponding absorption range in wavenumbers.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: State the reagent(s) needed for reaction $\mathbf{II}$.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction that occurs in reaction $\mathbf{III}$.

parts.label: (e)(iv)
parts.text:
The yield of reaction $\mathbf{I}$ is very low.

Explain why.
